อาคารไม่ได้คงรูปเดิมทั้งหมด สารานุกรมวัฒ: The buildings do not entirely retain their original forms. The Encyclopedia of Thai Culture states that the ordination hall once had a three-tiered roof covered with wooden shingles, but during repairs, it was reduced to a single tier and changed to galvanized iron. Another temple registry record indicates that the current preaching hall was built in 1963 (B.E. 2506) and lists the date of receiving the royal granting of the land for the ordination hall (Wisungkhammasima) as 8 January 1898 (B.E. 2440). However, some year details in secondary sources have printing or scanning errors, so they are not used as evidence to confirm other restoration years.
กรมศิลปากรขึ้นทะเบียนโบราณสถานของวัดใน พ: Krom Sinlapakon (Fine Arts Department) registered the temple as a historical site in 1996 (B.E. 2539), with its highlights being the surrounding wall and the large ordination hall with Chinese architectural influence. Later, in the context of the Takua Pa old town revitalization, the temple also houses the Takua Pa Community Museum, which collects utensils and equipment from the mining era. This makes the temple area serve as both a religious site and a space to recount the town's memories after the mining era.

Thetsaban Mueang Takua Pa (Takua Pa Town Municipality) has media introducing the temple, and in 2023 (B.E. 2566) published the candle procession · town circling activity along with a worshipping ceremony to request permission for the ordination hall restoration.

Academic works state that the museum keeps utensils and equipment from the mining era, making a visit to the temple connect with the town's labor, trade, and everyday life history.
